mainTopic: Does אביי's reading of the פסוק "מֵעִם מִזְבְּחִי" (that it is about a קרבן יחיד) hold up? A קל וחומר from יום טוב, and רבא's proof that the פסוק is about the תמיד.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of the פסוק "מֵעִם מִזְבְּחִי תִּקָּחֶנּוּ לָמוּת". אביי had read it as being about a כהן offering a קרבן יחיד. The גמרא attacks this reading with a קל וחומר from יום טוב. רבא then shows that "My altar" means the תמיד, so אביי's reading fails according to every opinion. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that money and purity cases begin with the greatest judge. It explains that רבי's court was an exception, because there the vote always started from the side. This leads to praise of רבי: from משה until רבי, no one person had unmatched תורה and worldly greatness for all his years. The גמרא tests this claim against יהושע, the kings and עזרא, and רב אדא בר אהבה extends it from רבי to רב אשי. Then the גמרא brings two sources for starting capital cases from the side: "לא תענה על ריב" and דוד girding his sword last. Finally, רב rules that a teacher may judge capital cases with his student, and a ברייתא that counts them as one vote challenges him. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from יום טוב against אביי's reading
steps.stepSummary: Execution does not push aside יום טוב. A קרבן יחיד does push aside יום טוב. So execution should certainly not push aside a קרבן יחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: A יום טוב gives way to an individual's offering, and still an execution does not push it aside. So an individual's offering, which is even stronger than יום טוב, should surely not be pushed aside by an execution!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי, who said the פסוק teaches that an execution pushes aside a כהן's קרבן יחיד. It builds a קל וחומר to show that this cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is a ranking. A קרבן יחיד is stronger than יום טוב, since it is brought even on יום טוב, and יום טוב is already too strong for an execution to push aside. So the even stronger קרבן יחיד should certainly not be pushed aside by an execution, which goes against אביי's reading of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A Festival day
An offering brought by an individual, not by the whole community
Here: executing a murderer by the court
Is pushed aside / pushes aside (overrides)
Is it not logical? (the classic wording of a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: Here רציחה does not mean committing murder. It means the court carrying out the death penalty on a murderer.

phrases.aramaic: מָה יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁנִּדְחֶה מִפְּנֵי קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד,
phrases.english: Just as a Festival, which is pushed aside for an individual's offering,
is not pushed aside by murder,
phrases.notes: He means the court does not execute a murderer on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד שֶׁהוּא דּוֹחֶה אֶת יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: then an individual's offering, which pushes aside a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא רְצִיחָה דּוֹחָה אוֹתוֹ?
phrases.english: is it not logical that murder should not push it aside?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁנִּדְחֶה מִפְּנֵי קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's explanation of the פסוק from just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that "מעם מזבחי" refers to a קרבן יחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if execution cannot push aside יום טוב, it surely cannot push aside a קרבן יחיד, which is stronger than יום טוב.

steps.title: The challenge only works according to one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר depends on individuals' offerings being brought on יום טוב. That is a מחלוקת, so the attack on אביי works only according to the view that they are brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי's reading is fine according to the view that vow and gift offerings are not brought on יום טוב. But according to the view that they are brought on יום טוב, what can be said for אביי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the challenge from step 1 rests on a disputed point. It works against אביי only according to one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If נדרים ונדבות are not brought on יום טוב, a קרבן יחיד does not push aside יום טוב, so the קל וחומר falls apart and אביי is safe. Only the opposing view makes the קל וחומר work and leaves אביי with no answer.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well
According to the one who says
Vow offerings and gift offerings (voluntary individual offerings)
Are offered
What is there to say? (there seems to be no answer)

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: that vow and gift offerings are not brought on a Festival,
but according to the one who says
that vow and gift offerings are brought on a Festival,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the challenge of step 1 by showing it depends on a מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading, according to the view that נדרים ונדבות are brought on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to that view the קל וחומר of step 1 is valid, so אביי's reading cannot stand.

steps.title: רבא: according to one view, the פסוק makes no sense at all
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that according to the view that individuals' offerings are brought on יום טוב, אביי's reading obviously fails, because the פסוק would have no meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: there is no need to say this according to the view that vow and gift offerings are brought on יום טוב, since then "from My altar" cannot be applied at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a stronger rejection of אביי using the pattern "no need to say... but even...". This step is the first half and sets up the bigger point in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a קרבן יחיד is strong enough to push aside יום טוב, the קל וחומר shows that an execution can never push aside any offering. Then the פסוק "מעם מזבחי" would have no case to apply to, so אביי's reading clearly fails according to this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (a new approach)
It is not necessary to say (the easy case comes first)
Cannot be applied / has no meaning
From My altar

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is not necessary to say this according to the one who says
that vow and gift offerings are brought on a Festival,
since then "from My altar" cannot be applied at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with step 2 about the second view, and prepares to go further.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's reading according to the view that נדרים ונדבות are brought on יום טוב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to that view the פסוק would have no case to apply to.

steps.title: Even according to the other view, "My altar" means the תמיד
steps.stepSummary: Even if individuals' offerings are not brought on יום טוב, "My altar" refers to the offering that belongs especially to ה׳, the תמיד. The תורה says to take the כהן even from that to be executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But even according to the view that vow and gift offerings are not brought on יום טוב, isn't it written "from My altar"? That means the offering set aside for Me. Which is that? The daily offering. And the Merciful One said: "From My altar you shall take him, to die."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his point. Even according to the view where the קל וחומר does not work, אביי is wrong, because the פסוק itself is talking about the תמיד, not a קרבן יחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the word "מזבחי", My altar, as pointing to the offering most closely tied to ה׳, which is the communal תמיד. Since the תורה says to take the כהן away even from the תמיד to be executed, the פסוק cannot be limited to a קרבן יחיד. So אביי's reading is rejected according to every opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Set aside especially for Me
The daily communal offering, brought every morning and afternoon
The Merciful One (a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the תורה)
You shall take him to die

steps.whatToRemember: רבא proves that "מעם מזבחי" refers to the תמיד, so אביי's reading (that it means a קרבן יחיד) fails according to every opinion. An execution pushes aside even the תמיד.

phrases.english: But even according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת אֵין קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: that vow and gift offerings are not brought on a Festival,
isn't it written "from My altar"?
"My altar" means the offering set aside for Me,
and which is that? The daily offering.
And the Merciful One said:
"From My altar you shall take him, to die."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's "not necessary... but even" argument from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's reading according to every opinion
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: "מזבחי" refers to the תמיד, so the פסוק cannot be limited to a קרבן יחיד.

steps.title: רב says they started with him in רבי's court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about which judge speaks first in money and purity cases. רב reports that in רבי's court, the voting began with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: in monetary cases and in cases of impurity and purity, they begin with the greatest judge. רב said: I was among the judges counted in רבי's court, and they would begin with me first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new piece of the משנה and brings רב's personal memory about how voting worked in רבי's court. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that in דיני ממונות and טומאה וטהרה the greatest judge speaks first. רב was a junior judge in רבי's court, yet he says they started with him. That looks like it goes against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Monetary cases
Questions of ritual impurity and purity
The count of judges; the group of judges whose votes are counted
The court or study hall of רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: Monetary cases, impurities and purities, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The rest of it says that in these cases they begin with the greatest judge.

phrases.english: Rav said:
I was among the counted judges of the school of Rabbi,
and with me myself they would begin first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אֲנָא הֲוַאי בְּמִנְיָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה, separate from the קרבן discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי's court, the voting began with רב, a junior judge.

steps.title: But the משנה says to start with the greatest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's report, because the משנה says to begin with the greatest judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: 'They begin with the greatest'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי's court could start with רב, since the משנה says money and purity cases begin with the greatest judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was not the greatest judge in רבי's court. So if they started with him, it seems they broke the משנה's rule. The גמרא needs to explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: They begin with the greatest judge

phrases.english: But we,
learned: 'They begin with the greatest'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן מַתְחִילִין מִן הַגָּדוֹל תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's report from the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that voting began with him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires money and purity cases to begin with the greatest judge, and רב was a junior judge.

steps.title: רבי's court always began from the side
steps.stepSummary: רבה son of רבא, or some say רבי הלל son of רבי וולס, explains that רבי's court was different: they began from the side in every count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה son of רבא said, and some say it was רבי הלל son of רבי וולס: The count in רבי's court was different, because in all their counts they would begin from the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי's court had a special practice. In every kind of case, voting started with the junior judges on the side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule for money cases still stands in general. רבי's court is an exception. It used the start-from-the-side method, which the משנה uses for דיני נפשות, in all cases. That is why רב, a junior judge, spoke first.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
From the side, meaning starting with the junior judges

phrases.english: Rabba son of Rava said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי הִלֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי וָולֶס:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Valles:
The count of the school of Rabbi is different,
because all of their counts,
they would begin from the side.
phrases.notes: 'From the side' means the junior judges, who sat at the ends. In the משנה, this is the method for capital cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception: a special practice of one court
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's court went against the משנה's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's court began every count from the side, so starting with רב was its normal practice.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule is to start money cases with the greatest judge. רבי's court was an exception and always started from the side.

steps.title: No one combined תורה and greatness from משה until רבי
steps.stepSummary: The same אמורא praises רבי: from משה until רבי, nobody combined תורה greatness and worldly greatness in one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה son of רבא said, and some say it was רבי הלל son of רבי וולס: From the days of משה until רבי, we do not find תורה and greatness in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא mentioned רבי's special court, it brings another statement by the same speaker about how unique רבי was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Torah and greatness in one place' means that one person was both the top תורה scholar of his generation and a top worldly leader. The claim is that only משה and רבי had both. This claim gets tested in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: תורה greatness together with worldly greatness, such as wealth and leadership
In one place, meaning in one person
We do not find

phrases.english: And Rabba son of Rava said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי הִלֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי וָולֶס:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Valles:
From the days of Moshe until Rabbi,
we do not find Torah and greatness
in one place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related statement from the same speaker about רבי's greatness
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Between משה and רבי, nobody combined unmatched תורה and unmatched worldly greatness.

steps.title: What about יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim: יהושע seems to have had both תורה and greatness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And was there not? But there was יהושע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether יהושע breaks the rule, since he led the nation and was also a great תורה scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע came after משה and before רבי, and he was the leader of the Jewish people. If he was also the top תורה authority, the claim that nobody combined both would be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: משה's student and the next leader of the Jewish people
And was there not?

phrases.english: And was there not? But there was Yehoshua!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of step 8 with a counterexample
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no one between משה and רבי combined תורה and greatness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יהושע was the leader and a great תורה scholar, so he seems to have had both.

steps.title: אלעזר was there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in יהושע's time there was אלעזר, who was equal to him in תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that יהושע was not alone at the top in תורה, because אלעזר הכהן was his equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim means unmatched תורה greatness. Since אלעזר was as great as יהושע in תורה, the 'תורה' part was not found in יהושע alone.

keyTerms.meaning: אלעזר הכהן, son of אהרן

phrases.english: There was Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from יהושע
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies that the claim means unmatched greatness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהושע had both kinds of greatness.
steps.terutzMaskana: אלעזר was equal to יהושע in תורה, so יהושע's תורה greatness was not unmatched.

steps.title: What about פנחס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: פנחס, who lived after אלעזר, could be the one who had both.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was פנחס!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another possible example. After אלעזר died, פנחס might have been unmatched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer about אלעזר works only while אלעזר was alive. פנחס came after him, so he might have stood alone with both kinds of greatness.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of אלעזר, who lived after him

phrases.english: But there was Pinchas!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new counterexample after the answer about אלעזר
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of step 8, after the answer about אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פנחס lived after אלעזר, so no one may have equaled him.

steps.title: The זקנים were there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in פנחס's time there were the זקנים, who were equal to him in תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were the Elders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that פנחס was not unmatched either, because the זקנים of his time were his equals in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same pattern repeats: another person or group matched the possible example in תורה. So the claim about רבי still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The Elders, the great leaders and scholars of that generation

phrases.english: There were the Elders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from פנחס
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies that the claim means unmatched greatness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פנחס had both kinds of greatness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The זקנים were equal to פנחס in תורה.

steps.title: What about King שאול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim using שאול, who was both king and a great person.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was שאול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another possible exception: שאול was king. Didn't he combine תורה and greatness?
steps.deeperAnalysis: After יהושע and פנחס were answered, the גמרא moves on to the first king. שאול held the highest worldly power, so if nobody matched him in תורה, the claim about רבי would be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But there was (a challenge naming someone)
Saul, the first king of ישראל
Greatness, meaning worldly power and leadership

phrases.english: But there was Saul!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer about פנחס, the גמרא tries a new candidate from a later period.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 8 that nobody between משה and רבי had both תורה and greatness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שאול was king and also great, so he seems to be a counterexample.

steps.title: שמואל was equal to him in תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל lived in שאול's time and matched him in תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: שאול was not unique, because שמואל was there too and was equal to him in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim requires one person to be the top in BOTH areas with nobody equal. Since שמואל matched שאול in תורה, שאול was not alone at the top.

keyTerms.meaning: Samuel the prophet, who anointed שאול

phrases.english: There was Samuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from שאול.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שאול stood alone at the top in both areas.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל was his equal in תורה, so שאול was not unique.

steps.title: But שמואל died during שאול's reign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: שמואל died while שאול was still king, so for a time שאול was alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. שמואל died before שאול did, so after that, שאול had nobody equal to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer from step 14 only works while שמואל was alive. Once שמואל died, שאול seems to have been the top in both areas, at least for his remaining years.

keyTerms.meaning: He died (literally, his soul rested)

phrases.english: But he died!
phrases.notes: "He" is שמואל, who died while שאול was still king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שמואל was שאול's equal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל died during שאול's reign, so after his death שאול had both areas alone.

steps.title: We mean all the years of his leadership
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the claim means being unique for one's entire time as leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about all his years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies what the original claim means: being the only one with both qualities for ALL the years of one's leadership, not just for part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a stricter standard. שאול had שמואל as an equal for part of his reign, so he was not unique for all of it, while רבי was unique the whole time.

keyTerms.meaning: All of his years
We are saying, meaning this is what we meant

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is ignoring שמואל's death. It admits that שאול was alone for a while, but says the claim is about being alone for the WHOLE time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer becomes the standard reply for the rest of the list, whenever the equal person dies or is killed.

phrases.english: We are speaking about all his years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about שמואל's death.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the scope of the original claim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The claim might be broken if someone was unique even for part of his reign.
steps.terutzMaskana: The claim means unique for all the years of leadership, and שאול was not.

steps.title: What about King דוד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges using דוד, who was both king and a great תורה figure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was דוד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another king: דוד. Wasn't he the top in both תורה and power?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the גמרא moves to שאול's successor. דוד was famous for both kingship and תורה, so he seems like a strong counterexample.

keyTerms.meaning: King David

phrases.english: But there was David!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After שאול is answered, the גמרא tries the next king.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דוד was king and a great תורה figure, so he seems to have had both.

steps.title: עירא היאירי was equal to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עירא היאירי matched דוד in תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was עירא היאירי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: דוד was not alone, because עירא היאירי was his equal in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is the same pattern as before: an equal in תורה means the king was not unique in both areas.

keyTerms.meaning: Ira the Yairite, a person from דוד's time

phrases.english: There was Ira the Yairite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from דוד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דוד stood alone at the top in both areas.
steps.terutzMaskana: עירא היאירי was his equal in תורה.

steps.title: But עירא died during דוד's reign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that עירא died while דוד was still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same kind of challenge: עירא died first, so for a while דוד was alone at the top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same attack as in step 15, now applied to עירא.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But he died!
phrases.notes: "He" is עירא, who died during דוד's lifetime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that עירא was דוד's equal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After עירא's death, דוד had nobody equal to him.

steps.title: Again: all the years
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: the claim means being unique for one's whole leadership.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about all his years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as in step 16: דוד was not unique for ALL his years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since עירא was equal to דוד for part of his reign, דוד does not meet the standard of being alone the entire time.

keyTerms.meaning: His years

phrases.english: We are speaking about all his years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 with the rule set in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דוד was alone after עירא died.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was not alone for all his years, so the claim stands.

steps.title: What about King שלמה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges using שלמה, the wisest of kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was שלמה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the next king, שלמה, who was famous for wisdom and power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה is perhaps the strongest candidate yet, since he was known as the wisest of all people and ruled a great kingdom.

keyTerms.meaning: King Solomon, son of דוד

phrases.english: But there was Solomon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After דוד is answered, the גמרא tries his son.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמה had both wisdom and kingship.

steps.title: שמעי בן גרא was equal in תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמעי בן גרא lived in שלמה's time and was great in תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was שמעי בן גרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: שמעי בן גרא was there, so שלמה was not alone at the top in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is the same pattern again: a contemporary of the king's level in תורה breaks the king's uniqueness.

keyTerms.meaning: Shimi son of Gera, a man from the time of דוד and שלמה

phrases.english: There was Shimi ben Gera.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from שלמה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלמה stood alone at the top in both areas.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמעי בן גרא was great in תורה in his time.

steps.title: But שלמה killed him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that שלמה had שמעי killed, so afterward שלמה was alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he killed him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: שלמה put שמעי to death, so for the rest of his reign שלמה had no equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the equal did not just die. שלמה himself had him killed. Either way, שלמה was then left alone at the top.

keyTerms.meaning: He killed him

phrases.english: But he killed him!
phrases.notes: שלמה had שמעי put to death; see מלכים א 2:46.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שמעי was שלמה's equal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once שמעי was killed, שלמה had no equal.

steps.title: Again: all the years
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: שלמה was not unique for his whole reign.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about all his years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers as before: the claim is about being alone for ALL the years of one's leadership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While שמעי was alive, שלמה had an equal, so he was not alone the whole time.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it

phrases.english: We are speaking about all his years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 with the standard from step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלמה was alone after שמעי was killed.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was not alone for all his years.

steps.title: What about King חזקיה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges using חזקיה, a righteous king known for spreading תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was חזקיה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא jumps forward to King חזקיה. Wasn't he the top in both תורה and kingship?
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה was a king who was also a great תורה leader, so he seems like another possible exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Hezekiah, a righteous king of יהודה

phrases.english: There was Hezekiah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After שלמה is answered, the גמרא tries a later king.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חזקיה was both king and a great תורה figure.

steps.title: שבנא was equal to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שבנא matched חזקיה in תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was שבנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: שבנא lived then and was חזקיה's equal in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again, a contemporary equal in תורה means the king was not unique.

keyTerms.meaning: Shebna, a great man in חזקיה's time

phrases.english: There was Shebna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from חזקיה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה stood alone at the top.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבנא was his equal in תורה.

steps.title: But שבנא was killed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that שבנא was killed during חזקיה's reign.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he was killed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: שבנא was killed, so afterward חזקיה was alone at the top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same attack as with שמואל, עירא and שמעי: once the equal is gone, the king seems unique.

keyTerms.meaning: He was killed

phrases.english: But he was killed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שבנא was חזקיה's equal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After שבנא was killed, חזקיה had no equal.

steps.title: Again: all the years
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: חזקיה was not unique for his whole reign.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about all his years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers once more that the claim is about ALL the years of one's leadership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because שבנא was equal to חזקיה for part of his reign, חזקיה does not meet the standard.

keyTerms.meaning: We say

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern for each king: (1) Wasn't he unique? (2) No, someone was equal in תורה. (3) But that person died. (4) The claim means unique for ALL his years.

phrases.english: We are speaking about all his years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 with the standard from step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה was alone after שבנא's death.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was not alone for all his years.

steps.title: What about עזרא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges using עזרא, the great תורה leader of the return from Babylonia.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was עזרא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more candidate: עזרא, who led the people and was the greatest תורה scholar of his day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא was not a king, but he was the leader of the people as well as the top תורה authority, so he also seems to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Ezra the scribe, leader of the return to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: But there was Ezra!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After חזקיה is answered, the גמרא tries a leader from the Second Temple period.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עזרא was both the leader and the top תורה scholar.

steps.title: נחמיה was equal to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that נחמיה בן חכליה lived in עזרא's time and was his equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was נחמיה בן חכליה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: עזרא was not alone, because נחמיה בן חכליה was his equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same answer pattern keeps the original claim safe: every great leader before רבי had someone equal to him at least for part of his leadership.

keyTerms.meaning: Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, a leader in עזרא's time

phrases.english: There was Nehemiah son of Hacaliah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from עזרא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עזרא stood alone at the top in both areas.
steps.terutzMaskana: נחמיה בן חכליה was his equal, so עזרא was not unique.

steps.title: No one matched רב אשי in both תורה and greatness
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says that from the days of רבי until רב אשי, no one else had both top-level תורה and גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה says: I too say that from the days of רבי until רב אשי, we never found תורה and greatness together in one person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה adds his own statement in the same style as the earlier one about משה and רבי. He extends the idea to a later time period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statement said that between משה and רבי, no one besides them had both. רב אדא בר אהבה makes a matching claim for רבי through רב אשי. In this period, too, no one combined both, except רבי and רב אשי themselves, who stand at the two ends of the period.

keyTerms.meaning: תורה greatness together with worldly greatness (wealth and high position)
In one place, meaning in a single person
I too say, adding a similar statement of my own

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava says:
I too say,
phrases.notes: He means: I have a statement just like the earlier one about משה and רבי.

phrases.english: from the days of Rabbi until Rav Ashi
we have not found Torah and greatness
in one place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel statement covering a later era, after the challenges to the earlier statement were answered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From רבי until רב אשי, no one other than רבי and רב אשי themselves had both unmatched תורה and גדולה.

steps.title: Challenge from הונא בר נתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: wasn't there הונא בר נתן, who had both תורה and wealth?
steps.simpleTranslation: And was there not? But there was הונא בר נתן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה by pointing to a person from רב אשי's time who seemed to have both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הונא בר נתן was known as both a scholar and an important, wealthy man. If he had both, then רב אשי was not unique, and the statement looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And was there not? A challenge question
But there was, introducing a counter-example

phrases.english: And was there not?
But there was Huna bar Natan!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָא הֲוָה הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement of step 31 with a counter-example.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's claim that no one in that period matched רב אשי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A contemporary of רב אשי seems to have had both תורה and גדולה, so רב אשי was not unique.

steps.title: הונא בר נתן was below רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that הונא בר נתן was subordinate to רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: הונא בר נתן was subordinate to רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that הונא בר נתן did not really equal רב אשי. He accepted רב אשי's authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim was never that no one else had any תורה or wealth. It was that no one matched the leader. Since הונא בר נתן bowed to רב אשי, he was not his equal, so the statement stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He was subordinate to him (literally, he was bending to him)

steps.whatToRemember: The statement is about who was at the very top. Someone who submits to the leader does not count as equal to him.

phrases.english: Huna bar Natan

phrases.aramaic: מִיכָּף הֲוָה כַּיִיף לֵיהּ לְרַב אָשֵׁי.
phrases.english: was subordinate to Rav Ashi.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן מִיכָּף הֲוָה כַּיִיף לֵיהּ לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the counter-example: he was not truly equal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הונא בר נתן had both, so רב אשי was not unique.
steps.terutzMaskana: הונא בר נתן was below רב אשי, so רב אשי remained unmatched.

steps.title: Source for starting from the side in capital cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that in capital cases voting starts from the side benches, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Capital cases begin from the side. From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes a line of the משנה and asks for the source of this rule, which sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "From the side" means the judges who sit at the side, who are the less important ones, give their opinions first. The גמרא wants to know where the תורה teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: Capital cases, where a life is at stake
From the side, meaning the lesser judges vote first
From where are these matters derived? A request for a source

phrases.english: Capital cases begin from the side.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה. The judges on the side benches, the less senior ones, speak first.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת מַתְחִילִין מִן הַצַּד. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic discussion and returns to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for having the lesser judges vote first in capital cases.

steps.title: Source from "לא תענה על ריב"
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר פפא reads the פסוק "לא תענה על ריב" as "do not answer against the master."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר פפא says: The verse states, "You shall not answer in a cause [ריב]." Read it as: you shall not answer against the master [רב].
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר פפא gives the source. He reads the word ריב as רב, "the master."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Judges tend not to disagree with the greatest judge. If he spoke first, the others would likely just follow him. So the lesser judges speak first and give honest, independent opinions, which matters most when a life is on the line.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not answer in a dispute (שמות 23:2), read here as about the master

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a deep concern in capital cases that every judge's vote be truly his own, so the accused gets a fair hearing.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Pappa says:
The verse states: "You shall not answer in a cause."
You shall not answer against the master.
phrases.notes: The word ריב is written without the letter י in the פסוק, so it can be read רב, the master.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר פָּפָּא: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק לא תענה על ריב, read as רב, teaches that judges should not have to speak against the greatest judge. So he speaks last.

steps.title: Second source from דוד and his men
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן brings a source from דוד, who girded his sword last.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה says in the name of רבי יוחנן: from here: "And דוד said to his men: Each man gird his sword. And each man girded his sword, and דוד also girded his sword."
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different source for the same rule. He uses the story of דוד preparing to punish נבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This was a matter of life and death, and דוד, the greatest of the group, girded his sword last, after his men. This is a model for judging capital cases with the greatest person going last.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, introducing a different source
Each man gird his sword

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana says in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: from here:
"And David said to his men:
Each man gird his sword.
And each man girded his sword,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, so the quote matches the פסוק exactly.

phrases.english: and David also girded his sword."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule as step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דוד, the greatest, acted last in a life-and-death matter, so in capital cases the greatest judge speaks last.

steps.title: A teacher may judge capital cases with his student
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person may teach his student and then sit with him as a fellow judge in capital cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: A person may teach his student and then judge capital cases together with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a new ruling: a student may sit next to his own teacher as a judge in capital cases, and his vote counts on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might worry that a student will just repeat his teacher's view, so his vote would not really be independent. רב says this is not a problem, and the student may serve as a full judge.

keyTerms.meaning: A person teaches his student
And judges together with him

phrases.english: Rav says:
A person may teach his student,
and judge capital cases with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about who may sit together as judges in capital cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A teacher and his student may sit together as two separate judges in capital cases.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא counting teacher and student as one
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that teacher and student count as two only in purity matters. In money, capital, lashes, and calendar cases they count as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: In matters of purity and impurity, a father and his son, or a teacher and his student, are counted as two. In money cases, capital cases, lashes cases, sanctifying the month, and making a leap year, a father and his son, or a teacher and his student, are counted as only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite: in capital cases, teacher and student count as just one vote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a teacher and student count as only one, the student is not an independent judge. That goes against רב, who let the student sit as a full judge in capital cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Matters of ritual purity and impurity
They are counted as two votes
Declaring the new month and adding a leap month to the year

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say a student may never sit as a judge. It is about counting votes: his vote is not counted as separate from his teacher's.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
In matters of purity and impurity,
a father and his son, a teacher and his student,
are counted as two.

phrases.aramaic: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת וְדִינֵי מַכּוֹת,
phrases.english: Money cases, capital cases, and cases of lashes,
sanctifying the month and making a leap year:
a father and his son, a teacher and his student,
are counted as only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling in step 37 from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a student may judge capital cases with his teacher.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא counts a teacher and his student as only one vote in capital cases, so the student is not an independent judge. That contradicts רב.
